connected.title: Four Modules, One Workflow
connected.desc: Information moves between correspondence, documents, meetings, and business processes within a single flow, with every step remaining connected to its related information and processes.
connected.note: This order is one example, not a fixed path. Any module can start a process and any module can be called into one: a committee decision can open a new workflow, a workflow can generate outgoing correspondence, and every step writes back to the same record.

receive.title: Correspondence arrives
receive.desc: An incoming letter or request from an external entity is registered, given a reference number, matched to its sender, linked to its attachments, and routed to the responsible department.

centralize.title: Information is centralized
centralize.desc: The attachments and supporting files behind that correspondence are stored in one controlled repository — versioned, permissioned, and available to every authorized team.

review.title: Review and approval begin
review.desc: The request enters its approval path — department review, management sign-off, final approval — with owners, deadlines, and a complete record of who acted and when.

decide.title: A decision needs a meeting
decide.desc: When a matter calls for deliberation, it moves onto a committee or department agenda. The meeting records the decision, the action items, and the teams responsible for them.

followUp.title: Follow-up returns to the workflow
followUp.desc: Action items raised in the meeting come back as tracked tasks with owners and due dates, so a decision is not closed until the work behind it is done.

preserve.title: The final record is preserved
preserve.desc: The approved document, the decision that produced it, and the full history — correspondence, versions, approvals, minutes — are retained together as one controlled organizational record.

hero.desc: ECM+ brings documents, correspondence, meetings, and business processes into one connected platform — designed for organizations where information moves across teams, departments, and decisions.

story.title: One connected record, not disconnected pieces
story.paragraph1: Over more than twenty years, ECM+ has built extensive experience managing organizations' information and processes across a wide range of sectors.
story.paragraph2: That experience shaped the ECM+ platform: a system that connects documents, correspondence, meetings, and business processes together in one scalable, customizable environment.

scale.title: Built for scale, not for spectacle
scale.desc: We build ECM+ to handle the volume of information and complexity of processes in large organizations, with the ability to scale as your organization's needs grow.

oneSystem.title: One platform, connected modules
oneSystem.desc: Each module operates as part of one system, so documents, correspondence, meetings, and business processes can connect and exchange information with one another.

governance.title: Security and governance from the start
governance.desc: We build access rights, permission management, information retention, and action tracking into the platform's design from the start, to keep information managed in an organized and accountable way.

leadership.name: Khaled Abdelal
leadership.bio: Khaled founded ECM+ with a focus on the structural challenges that arise when documents, decisions, and business processes become fragmented across an organization.

title.mainTitle: Manage your organization's documents from one place.

hero.desc: ECM+ DMS organizes and stores your organization's documents, and makes them searchable, accessible, and shareable, while managing permissions and retention policies throughout the document's lifecycle.

challenges.title: Before a document has a system, it has no reliable home.
challenges.desc: Most organizations don't lack documents — they lack a reliable way to find, control, and keep them.

finding.title: Finding a document means asking around
finding.desc: Files live on shared drives, personal desktops, and email attachments — finding the right version often means messaging three people before someone remembers where it went.

access.title: Sensitive files are one click away from anyone
access.desc: Without controlled access, HR records, contracts, and financial documents sit in folders that far more people can open than actually should.

versions.title: Old versions get mistaken for current ones
versions.desc: When a document is edited outside a controlled system, there's no reliable way to know which copy is the one that was actually approved.

retention.title: Nothing gets kept — or deleted — on purpose
retention.desc: Without a retention policy, documents accumulate indefinitely, or disappear when someone leaves the company with the only copy on their laptop.

lifecycle.title: From document intake to archiving or disposal.
lifecycle.desc: DMS manages the complete document lifecycle — from intake and organization, through access and use, to archiving or disposal according to organizational policy.

capture.title: Capture & Classify
capture.desc: Documents enter the system through upload, scanning, or integration, then are indexed and classified using defined metadata and document types.

organize.title: Organize & Govern
organize.desc: Folder structures, metadata, access policies, and document classifications are applied consistently, giving every document a defined and governed place.

collaborate.title: Access & Collaborate
collaborate.desc: Authorized users access, review, edit, and share documents under version control, with permissions, changes, and activity fully traceable.

retain.title: Retain & Dispose
retain.desc: Retention schedules and legal holds determine how long information remains available, with controlled disposition when retention requirements are fulfilled.

benefits.title: As documents multiply, your organization needs a clear way to manage them.
benefits.desc: With multiple files, departments, and users, document management helps organize information and make it easier to access, with greater clarity around permissions, versions, and retention policies.

retrieval.title: Every document, found in seconds
retrieval.desc: Teams stop losing time hunting for files — one search returns the current, correct version every time.

security.title: Sensitive information stays sensitive
security.desc: Role-based access means the right people see the right documents, automatically, without anyone having to police it manually.

compliance.title: Compliance becomes routine, not a project
compliance.desc: Retention and audit trails run in the background, so a regulatory request is a report, not a scramble.

singleTruth.title: One version of the truth, always
singleTruth.desc: Everyone works from the same current file, with a full history of who changed what and when.

connections.title: DMS doesn't work alone
connections.desc: A document archived here becomes the same record the rest of the platform relies on — not a copy that has to be kept in sync by hand.

cms.title: Feeds every correspondence
cms.desc: Attachments in CMS are the same documents governed by DMS's access and retention rules — not a separate, disconnected copy.

mms.title: Referenced in every meeting
mms.desc: Documents attached to a meeting stay linked to their original DMS record, agenda to archive.

bpm.title: Archived automatically from workflows
bpm.desc: A BPM process can write its output straight back into DMS as a workflow step — archived and retained without anyone filing it by hand.

title.mainTitle: Manage your organization's correspondence from one place.

hero.desc: ECM+ CMS organizes incoming and outgoing correspondence in one place — registering, classifying, routing, and tracking the actions related to it.

challenges.title: A letter without a system becomes a rumor about a letter.
challenges.desc: Correspondence that isn't tracked formally is only as reliable as whoever last remembered to update a spreadsheet.

logging.title: Incoming letters get logged in a spreadsheet — if at all
logging.desc: A received letter's status often depends on someone remembering to update a shared file, and that file usually lives on one person's computer.

status.title: No one can say where a reply actually stands
status.desc: A request sent out for review can sit untouched for weeks with no automatic reminder and no visibility into who's holding it up.

linking.title: Correspondence and the documents it references live apart
linking.desc: A letter approving a contract and the contract itself often end up in two different places, with nothing formally linking them together.

audit.title: An audit means digging through inboxes
audit.desc: When a regulator or auditor asks for a communication history, reconstructing it means searching individual mailboxes rather than pulling one record.

lifecycle.title: From registering correspondence to responding and closing it.
lifecycle.desc: CMS manages the complete correspondence lifecycle — from registration and classification, through routing and tracking related actions, to closing and archiving.

register.title: Register & Classify
register.desc: Incoming and outgoing correspondence is registered with reference details, sender or recipient information, classification, and linked attachments.

route.title: Route & Assign
route.desc: Correspondence is routed to the responsible department or individual, with ownership, deadlines, priorities, and escalation rules applied according to policy.

respond.title: Respond & Track
respond.desc: Replies, forwards, actions, and status changes are recorded against the original correspondence, maintaining a complete and traceable communication history.

close.title: Close & Archive
close.desc: Once resolved, correspondence is formally closed and retained as a searchable record, with related documents, decisions, and actions preserved together.

benefits.title: Clearer correspondence management, and more precise tracking of its actions.
benefits.desc: CMS helps organize correspondence and clarify the responsibilities and actions related to it, making it easy to refer back to each correspondence's record and its outcomes.

noDrops.title: No correspondence falls through the cracks
noDrops.desc: Every letter has an owner, a status, and a deadline the moment it's registered.

accountability.title: Accountability is visible, not assumed
accountability.desc: Anyone can see exactly who's holding up a response, and for how long.

connected.title: Documents and decisions stay connected
connected.desc: A letter and the contract it approved live in the same record, not two disconnected files.

fastAudits.title: Audits take hours, not weeks
fastAudits.desc: A full communication history is one query away, not a search through years of inboxes.

connections.title: CMS doesn't work alone
connections.desc: Correspondence here is never an island — it's tied to the documents, meetings, and approvals it actually relates to.

dms.title: Every attachment stays governed
dms.desc: A letter's attachments are DMS-controlled documents, not separate files — permissions and retention travel with them.

mms.title: Correspondence discussed in meetings stays linked
mms.desc: A letter referenced in a meeting keeps its full CMS history connected to that discussion.

bpm.title: Correspondence can trigger a workflow
bpm.desc: An incoming letter needing approval can hand off directly into a BPM process instead of being tracked by hand.

title.mainTitle: Manage meetings from agenda to follow-up.

hero.desc: ECM+ MMS organizes your organization's meetings — from preparing the agenda and inviting participants, to documenting minutes and decisions, to tracking the actions that result from each meeting.

challenges.title: A meeting without a system leaves no trace once it ends.
challenges.desc: What gets decided in a room is only real if it's written down somewhere everyone can find later.

scheduling.title: Meetings get booked by email, and double-booked anyway
scheduling.desc: Without a shared scheduling system, room and calendar conflicts get caught after invitations already went out — sometimes not at all.

decisions.title: Decisions exist only in someone's memory of the meeting
decisions.desc: Without a formal record, what a committee actually agreed to becomes a matter of whoever took the most complete notes.

actions.title: Action items get mentioned, then forgotten
actions.desc: A task assigned verbally in a meeting has no owner, no deadline, and no way to be followed up on once everyone leaves the room.

history.title: There's no record of what a committee has decided over time
history.desc: Looking back at a committee's history means searching through old emails and hoping someone forwarded the right thread.

lifecycle.title: From scheduling the meeting to following up on its decisions and actions.
lifecycle.desc: MMS manages the complete meeting lifecycle — from preparation and convening, through documenting decisions, to tracking the resulting actions and tasks.

schedule.title: Schedule & Prepare
schedule.desc: Meetings are scheduled with participants, agendas, topics, and supporting documents organized in advance to ensure every session begins with the right context.

convene.title: Convene & Discuss
convene.desc: Attendance, discussion points, notes, and topic progress are captured during the meeting, creating a structured record of what was discussed.

decide.title: Decide & Record
decide.desc: Decisions are formally recorded against their originating topics, preserving the rationale and outcomes as part of the meeting record.

followUp.title: Follow Up & Close
followUp.desc: Action items are assigned with accountable owners and due dates, tracked through completion, and linked back to the meeting that created them.

benefits.title: Turn meeting outcomes into trackable information and actions.
benefits.desc: MMS brings meeting details, decisions, and follow-up actions together in one record, making it easy to look back at what was agreed and track what happens after the meeting ends.

decisions.title: Organized meetings from the start
decisions.desc: Meeting schedules, participants, agendas, and related resources are managed through an organized process before the meeting takes place.

ownedTasks.title: Clear documentation of meeting decisions
ownedTasks.desc: Decisions are recorded in the meeting minutes, becoming a clear reference instead of relying on personal notes or memory.

history.title: Tracking tasks and responsibilities
history.desc: Action items from the meeting are linked to their owners and due dates, making follow-up part of the workflow after the meeting ends.

scheduling.title: A unified record of meetings and decisions
scheduling.desc: Meeting minutes, decisions, and actions stay preserved in an organized record, making it easy to look back at meeting history and track what was previously decided.

connections.title: MMS doesn't work alone
connections.desc: What happens in a meeting doesn't stay in the meeting — it flows straight into the rest of the platform.

dms.title: Meeting files are archived, not lost
dms.desc: Documents attached to a meeting are stored under DMS's rules — searchable and retained after the meeting ends.

cms.title: Decisions become correspondence
cms.desc: A meeting outcome that needs to go out as a formal letter can move directly into CMS without re-entering it.

bpm.title: Action items become tracked processes
bpm.desc: A task assigned in a meeting can escalate into a full BPM workflow when it needs more than one approval step.

title.mainTitle: From process design to execution and monitoring.

hero.desc: ECM+ BPM lets you design, automate, execute, and monitor business processes through clear workflows — distributing tasks, managing approvals, and tracking the progress of each process.

challenges.title: A process without a system runs on whoever remembers the steps.
challenges.desc: Approvals that move by memory and email don't scale, and they don't leave a record when something goes wrong.

routing.title: Approvals move by email, one forward at a time
routing.desc: A request routed manually depends on each person remembering to pass it along — and stalls completely the moment someone is out of office.

visibility.title: No one can see where a request actually is
visibility.desc: Once something is submitted, tracking it down means asking around department by department until someone admits it's sitting in their inbox.

consistency.title: The same process runs differently depending on who's handling it
consistency.desc: Without a standardized workflow, two people submitting the same type of request can go through entirely different approval paths.

bottlenecks.title: Bottlenecks only show up after they've caused delay
bottlenecks.desc: There's no visibility into where requests pile up, so a slow step in the process isn't discovered until someone complains.

lifecycle.title: From process design to performance tracking and improvement.
lifecycle.desc: BPM manages the complete process lifecycle — from designing the workflow and its rules, through executing tasks and approvals, to monitoring performance and identifying improvement opportunities.

design.title: Design & Configure
design.desc: Workflows, forms, business rules, and approval paths are configured visually and aligned with organizational policies before being published for execution.

initiate.title: Initiate & Route
initiate.desc: A request enters the process and is routed automatically according to defined rules, responsibilities, conditions, and organizational structures.

execute.title: Approve & Execute
execute.desc: Tasks, approvals, decisions, and required actions are executed and recorded at every stage, with deadlines, escalations, and accountability enforced throughout the process.

monitor.title: Monitor & Improve
monitor.desc: Process performance, cycle times, bottlenecks, workload, and outcomes are monitored continuously, enabling process owners to identify improvements and refine workflows.

benefits.title: More organized processes, and clearer visibility into every stage.
benefits.desc: BPM helps standardize workflows, clarify responsibilities, and track process progress, while keeping a clear record of actions and decisions at every stage.

speed.title: Smoother process execution
speed.desc: Tasks and requests move to the next responsible person according to the defined workflow, reducing reliance on manual routing and follow-up.

visibility.title: Processes that run by clear rules
visibility.desc: The status of a process can be tracked at any time, showing the current stage, remaining tasks, and where delays are occurring.

consistency.title: Consistent application of procedures
consistency.desc: Processes are executed according to predefined paths and rules, helping standardize how requests and recurring procedures are handled.

record.title: A clear record of actions and decisions
record.desc: Actions, approvals, and decisions related to the process are preserved, making it easy to review what was done and identify responsibilities at each stage.

connections.title: BPM doesn't work alone

Document Organization: Organize documents within folders and subfolders.
Folder Navigation: Browse folders and access their contents easily.
File Management: Upload, move, copy, and manage files within folders.
Sharing: Share folders and their contents with authorized users.
Access Control: Manage permissions for folders and their contents.
Search: Search for documents and folders within the explorer.
Preview: Preview supported documents and files directly from the explorer.

search.featureShortDesc: Find documents quickly using powerful search and filters.
featureDesc: Global Search: Search across documents and archived content.
Keyword Search: Find documents using keywords and phrases.
Advanced Filters: Filter results by type, date, status, classification, and other fields.
Metadata Search: Search using document metadata and custom fields.
Saved Searches: Save frequently used search criteria for quick access.
Search Results: View relevant documents with key information and metadata.
Sorting: Sort results by date, name, type, relevance, and other criteria.

documentTypes.featureShortDesc: Create and configure document types and their required information.
featureDesc: Type Management: Create, edit, and manage document types.
Custom Fields: Define fields and information required for each type.
Type Classification: Organize documents according to predefined categories.
Field Configuration: Configure field types, requirements, and validation.
Templates: Associate document templates with specific document types.
Permissions: Control access to document types and their configurations.
Type Status: Enable or disable document types when needed.

aclPolicies.featureShortDesc: Control document access through flexible permission policies.
featureDesc: Access Policies: Create and manage document access policies.
User Permissions: Grant or restrict access for specific users.
Group Permissions: Assign permissions to groups, departments, or roles.
Permission Levels: Control actions such as viewing, editing, sharing, downloading, and deleting.
Inheritance: Apply permissions across folders and their contents.
Access Restrictions: Restrict sensitive documents to authorized users.
Policy Management: Update and manage access policies as organizational requirements change.

retentionRules.featureShortDesc: Define how long documents are retained and when they are archived or disposed.
featureDesc: Retention Policies: Create and manage document retention rules.
Retention Periods: Define how long documents should be retained.
Document Types: Apply retention rules to specific document types or categories.
Automatic Archiving: Automatically archive documents based on defined rules.
Expiration Management: Identify documents approaching or reaching their retention limit.
Disposal Rules: Define actions for documents after their retention period.
Compliance: Support organizational and regulatory document retention requirements.

sharedDocuments.featureShortDesc: Access and manage documents shared with users and teams.
featureDesc: Shared Documents: View documents shared with you or your teams.
Document Sharing: Share documents with authorized users and groups.
Access Control: Define permissions for shared documents.
Shared Folders: Share folders and their contents with selected users.
Collaboration: Allow authorized users to work with shared documents.
Activity Tracking: Track sharing and document activities.
Remove Access: Revoke access to previously shared documents.

recycleBin.featureShortDesc: Manage deleted documents and restore them when needed.
featureDesc: Deleted Documents: View documents and files moved to the recycle bin.
Restore: Restore deleted documents to their original location.
Permanent Delete: Permanently remove documents when authorized.
Search & Filters: Find deleted documents using search and filtering options.
Deletion Details: View information about when and by whom a document was deleted.
Bulk Actions: Restore or permanently delete multiple documents.
Access Control: Restrict recycle bin actions based on user permissions.

cms.moduleDesc: Manage, organize, and track incoming and outgoing correspondence through an integrated correspondence management system.

settings.featureShortDesc: Manage the basic settings and data used by the correspondence system.
featureDesc: Correspondence Types: Create and manage correspondence types and their required fields and information.
Correspondence Statuses: Create and manage correspondence statuses used throughout the system.
Confidentiality Levels: Add and manage confidentiality levels for correspondence.
Priority Levels: Add and manage correspondence priority levels.
Tags: Create and manage tags used to classify and organize correspondence.
Receiving Methods: Define and manage the methods used to receive correspondence.

externalEntities.featureShortDesc: Manage external entities used for sending and receiving correspondence.
featureDesc: Add External Entity: Create and add external entities that the organization communicates with.
Basic Information: Store the entity name, description, address, and image.
Contacts: Add and manage contacts associated with each external entity.
Entity Management: View, edit, and manage external entity information.

correspondenceInbox.featureShortDesc: Manage incoming, outgoing, draft, and completed correspondence.
featureDesc: Incoming Correspondence: View and manage incoming correspondence and follow up on related actions.
Outgoing Correspondence: View and manage correspondence that has been sent.
Drafts: Save and manage correspondence that has not been completed or sent.
Completed Correspondence: Access correspondence for which all required actions have been completed.
Correspondence Actions: Perform available actions on correspondence based on its status and user permissions.

addCorrespondence.featureShortDesc: Create a new correspondence and enter all related information and attachments.
featureDesc: Basic Information: Enter the basic information of the correspondence.
Correspondence Type Information: Enter the information and fields specific to the selected correspondence type.
Attachments: Add files and documents related to the correspondence.
Email Attachments: Add files and attachments received through email.

mms.moduleDesc: Manage meetings, committees, tasks, and all related activities through an integrated meeting management platform.

performanceIndicators.featureShortDesc: Monitor meeting and task performance through clear statistics and indicators.
featureDesc: Meeting Statistics: View personal meeting statistics and overall meeting statistics.
Total Meetings: View the total number of meetings.
Meeting Status: Monitor upcoming, completed, draft, cancelled, and rescheduled meetings.
Task Inbox: View total, pending, in-progress, completed, and overdue tasks.
Weekly Meetings: View meetings scheduled during the current week.
Recent Meetings: Access recently created or completed meetings.
Calendar: View and manage meetings through the calendar.
Scheduling: Schedule meetings by selecting suitable dates and times.

settings.featureShortDesc: Manage buildings, meeting rooms, and related meeting series.
featureDesc: Add Building: Add buildings where meetings can be held.
Add Room: Add meeting rooms, link each room to its building, and enter its details.
Room Details: Define room information, location within the building, and capacity.
Related Meeting Series: Create and manage meeting series to link related meetings.

committees.featureShortDesc: Create and manage committees and their members for meeting participation.
featureDesc: Create Committee: Create a new committee and add its name, description, and members.
Committee Members: Add and manage committee members.
Committee List: View available committees when selecting meeting participants.
Invite Committee: Select an entire committee and add it to the meeting attendee list.

meetings.featureShortDesc: Create, manage, and monitor meetings and all related activities.
featureDesc: Create Meeting: Create a new meeting or link it to another meeting within a related meeting series.
Basic Information: Enter the meeting subject, description, date, start time, end time, meeting type, and time zone.
Meeting Type: Define whether the meeting is physical or online.
Physical Meetings: Select an available room and view its location within the building and capacity.
Online Meetings: Select a meeting platform and automatically create a meeting link or add one manually.
Organizer: The meeting creator is automatically assigned as the organizer, with the option to change the organizer.
Attendees: Add employees, employee groups, committee members, or external participants.
Agenda: Add meeting agenda items, assign presenters, and define the duration of each item.
Attachments: Add and manage meeting-related files with editing capabilities.
Tasks: Add tasks related to the meeting and define task details, assignee, priority, and due date.
Task Management: Delete created tasks, view task details, and update the status of the user's own tasks.
Meeting Invitations: Send meeting invitations to participants through the system.
Voting: Create a vote, add its name and description, define voting options, and select eligible voters.
Attendance Confirmation: Confirm participant attendance after the meeting.
Meeting Report: Create a meeting report and add details and outcomes from the meeting.
Attendance Signatures: Add signatures from selected participants to confirm their attendance.
Report Export: Export the meeting report as a PDF file.
Report Editing: Add and edit information within the meeting report.
Meeting Chat: Provide a dedicated conversation for meeting participants while keeping the conversation as part of the meeting record.
Meeting Tracking: View all meetings, access their details, and filter them based on meeting information.

taskInbox.featureShortDesc: Track user-related tasks and manage their status.
featureDesc: Task List: View all tasks related to meetings.
Task Status: View tasks that have not started, are in progress, or are completed.
Status Updates: Users can update the status of their own tasks only.
Task Permissions: Users can view all tasks but cannot modify the status of tasks assigned to other users.

bpm.moduleDesc: A system for managing and automating corporate processes, from designing and defining processes and forms, through publishing and running them, to assigning tasks and monitoring execution.

inbox.featureShortDesc: Manage assigned tasks and complete business process activities from one workspace.
featureDesc: My Tasks: View tasks currently assigned to the signed-in user.
Follow Up: Monitor tasks delegated to other employees while continuing to follow their progress.
Completed Tasks: View tasks that have already been completed.
Task Forms: Open the exact form configured for each process step.

Task Actions: Five distinct actions — assign (delegate) a task to another employee, reject a delegation you received, withdraw a delegation you made, reject the task itself, or return it one step in the process.
Shared Queue: Claim unassigned tasks from a shared work queue.
Search & Filters: Find tasks using free-text search and filters such as process, date range, originator, and participant.
Task Status: Track tasks through states such as in the queue, assigned, being worked, completed, delegated, escalated, rejected, and sent back a step.

services.featureShortDesc: Start business processes from a catalog containing only the services available to the current user.
featureDesc: Service Catalog: Display the processes that the current user is authorized to start; an empty catalog tells the user no process has been granted to them.
Published Processes: Show each process using its latest published version.
Start Form: Open the process-specific form before creating a new case.
Attachments: Upload required files before the case is created.
Case Creation: Start a process case using its process key.
First Task Assignment: The workflow engine applies the first step's assignment rule and sends the resulting task to the appropriate Inbox.
Authorization: Process availability is determined by server-side authorization.

definitions.featureShortDesc: Manage process definitions, versions, lifecycle status, and publication from the administration catalog.
featureDesc: Process Definitions: Manage all available process definitions.
Version Management: Maintain multiple versions of a process definition.
Draft: Keep processes in a draft state while they are being designed or modified.
Published: Publish a process version so it becomes available for starting new cases.
Retired: Retire processes that should remain available for records but should no longer be offered to users.
Current Version: Define the version that new cases will use.
Restore: Restore a retired process when it should become available again — retiring or restoring applies to the process as a whole, not a single version.
Running Cases: Existing cases continue executing the version they started with, even when a newer version is published.

studio.featureShortDesc: Design, configure, simulate, validate, and deploy business processes using a visual process designer.
featureDesc: Visual Designer: Draw business processes on a visual canvas without writing code.
Process Elements: Configure start events, end events, timer events, boundary events, user tasks, gateways, and automated steps.
Step Configuration: Configure forms, assignment rules, deadlines, escalation, bilingual summaries, and notifications for each step.

Assignment Rules: Assign steps using one of nine rule types — specific employee, work group, organisational unit, job title, direct manager, department manager, manager of a named unit, originator of the request, or a captured process value — with exactly one reference filled per rule.
Automated Steps: Configure email, WhatsApp, PDF generation, external services, database queries, and repository archiving.
Branching: Configure exclusive, parallel, and inclusive process gateways.
Simulation: Run a token through the diagram before deployment, prompting for the initial assignee and variables and opening each step's real form.
Validation: Detect blocking errors, which refuse the deploy, and warnings, which do not, before a process is deployed.
Deployment: Convert the configured process into an executable workflow contract and publish it as a version.

Business-Logic Pipeline: Turn the canvas into an engine-ready contract through validation, diagram emission, placeholder rewriting, condition compilation, variable cataloging, contract assembly, and version publishing — every step has an exact inverse, which is what makes a published process editable.
Re-opening: Open an existing published definition in the editor, modify it, and deploy the changes as a new version.
Deadlines & Escalation: Configure step-specific permitted durations and escalation targets, which can be resolved dynamically from a value captured earlier in the process.
Bilingual Design: Maintain English and Arabic names, descriptions, case titles, and step summaries.

templates.featureShortDesc: Create reusable form schemas that can be shared across business process definitions.
featureDesc: Form Builder: Design reusable forms visually without hand-written code.
Shared Schema: Use one schema model for task forms, notification bodies, and generated PDFs.
Field Types: Support text, number, date, dropdown, rating, table, signature, file upload, attachment preview, employee picker, dynamic text, and other fields.
Dynamic Data: Populate fields from service calls or database queries when the form is filled.
Reusable Templates: Save schemas as reusable assets that can be shared by multiple process definitions.
Runtime Rendering: Use the same form renderer for simulations, process start forms, and Inbox task forms.

monitoring.featureShortDesc: Monitor running process cases, execution progress, task ownership, history, and administrative actions.
featureDesc: Graphical Monitoring: View the case's process diagram together with its execution trace.
Execution Status: Identify activities that have already run, the current activity, and the person responsible for each task.
Detailed History: View the assignee, state, timing, and sequence of every activity.
Case Tracking: Follow a running case from the task where it is already being worked.
Suspend & Resume: Administrators can suspend and resume running cases according to engine state rules, recording a reason for the action.
Delete Case: Administrators can delete running cases when permitted by the engine, recording a reason for the action.
Start Form History: Re-open the original submitted start form in read-only mode.
Auditability: Preserve task actions, decisions, assignees, timing, and reasons throughout process execution.
